title: Daladala za Sabasaba Dodoma Zagoma
scope: Reported local transport-service stoppage by daladala drivers and owners at the Sabasaba stand in Dodoma. The article does not establish that they formed a physically assembled public group or give a human turnout count.
participants_original: The report describes daladala drivers and owners at the Sabasaba stand stopping service. It gives no human turnout; the more-than-3,000 figure concerns vehicles in a fee calculation, not participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The report establishes a service stoppage at the stand on 13 January, but does not describe a public gathering or provide a count or qualitative crowd-size estimate.

start_date.summary: The report explicitly dates the service stoppage to Wednesday, 13 January 2021. It does not establish that a public group physically assembled that day, so physical onset remains unknown and start_date is null.

end_date.summary: The article reports the stoppage that day but does not state when the service resumed or the protest physically ended.

location.summary: The report identifies the Sabasaba stand in Dodoma.

scope.summary: The article describes drivers and owners at the Sabasaba stand stopping daladala service, but does not verify a public group assembly, human attendance, or broader coordination.

organizer.summary: No formal organizer is named. A driver and owner, Abdul Mohammed, is quoted.

demands.summary: The account says drivers/owners objected to the small, poorly maintained stand, unclear station-versus-market use, daily fees, and vendors occupying parking space, and asked city leadership to improve conditions or allocate another site. The listed taxonomy has no direct infrastructure/terminal category; no explicit demand to reduce the fee is reported.

participants_original.summary: The report describes the actors and service stoppage but gives no human count or evidence that they assembled as a public crowd. Its more-than-3,000 figure concerns vehicles in a daily-fee calculation.

participants_min.summary: No human lower bound is reported.

participants_max.summary: No human upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No physical public gathering or human turnout is described; the service-stoppage report alone does not establish 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not describe violence by participants.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No negotiation or receipt of demands is reported.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beating response to this stoppage is reported.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No action to clear a crowd is reported.

state_response.ignore.summary: The city director declined to comment to the reporter; this does not establish avoidance of protesters or their demands.

state_response.killings.summary: No killing response to this stoppage is reported.

state_response.shootings.summary: No shooting response to this stoppage is reported.

title.summary: The candidate title follows the headline of the opened Global Publishers report.

notes: This is a documented transport-service stoppage reported for 13 January, but the article does not establish a physically assembled public group. The reported stoppage date is retained in field evidence and this note; physical start remains null and eligibility is pending_evidence. No inclusion is proposed. Keep the vehicle figure separate from attendance. The February 2 national truck/bus strike lead (TZ202101-S002) concerns alleged police brutality and gives no evidence of coordination with this local stand stoppage; do not merge them.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people physically assemble in public at the stand, and how many participated?
If a public assembly occurred, when did it physically begin? The article dates the service stoppage, not assembly onset.
Did the action include any public demonstration beyond suspending transport service at the stand?
When did the physical action end or transport service resume?
Can the infrastructure/terminal demand be mapped to an existing category without forcing a fit?
Is there independent contemporary coverage or a public local-government record? The Mwananchi, ITV and IPP Media leads are blocked and must not be retried or bypassed.
